description:
**Divergence** — newtypes in crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:
- `Id(String)` (private inner)
- `UTCDate(String)` (private inner)
- `Date(String)` (private inner)
- `State(String)` (private inner)
- `ValidationError(pub String)` (src/id.rs:10) — `pub` inner

The /review-workspace-api.md audit prompt explicitly calls out "Do newtypes have `pub` inner fields defeating type-safety?" as a flag-worthy axis.

**Caller-observable cost**: external code can write `let ValidationError(s) = err;` and bypass the Display/Error interface. The `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute on the type prevents struct-literal construction from outside the crate but does NOT prevent tuple-position destructuring once you have an instance. No outside-crate `.0` access exists today (verified by grep), so the divergence is currently latent.

**Maintainer cost**: inconsistent shape between `ValidationError` and the rest of the newtype family in the same file. Forces a future reader to ask "why is this one different?" with no documented reason.

**Note on intentional pub**: workspace AGENTS.md documents `pub extra: serde_json::Map<...>` as deliberately pub per "Caller contract — wire-key collisions". That justification does NOT apply to `ValidationError`'s pub-inner — there is no caller contract requiring outside-crate destructuring.

**Fix**: change `pub String` to `String` in crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:10. If callers were relying on `.0` access (verify with workspace grep), preserve through a `pub fn message(&self) -> &str` accessor.
title: jmap-types' ValidationError(pub String) has pub-inner; 4 sibling newtypes in the same crate use private inner — flag-worthy asymmetry per audit prompt
